steps.tx: During early development, the apex of the midgut loop communicates directly with the yolk sac through the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct within the umbilical cord. Normally, this connection obliterates completely by the sixth gestational week. Persistence of the proximal portion of this duct forms a **Meckel diverticulum**, the most common congenital anomaly of the gastrointestinal tract.
steps.say: Early in life, the midgut connects to the yolk sac through the vitelline duct in the umbilical cord. This duct normally atrophies by the sixth week. Persistence of its intestinal end creates a Meckel diverticulum, the most common congenital malformation of the digestive tract.

vis.alt: Vitelline duct connection to midgut loop and umbilical cord
vis.caption: Vitelline duct relationship to the embryonic ileum and umbilicus. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: A Meckel diverticulum adheres to the classic Rule of Twos: it occurs in two percent of the population, is located within two feet (fifty centimeters) of the ileocecal valve, measures two inches in length, contains two types of ectopic mucosa (heterotopic gastric or pancreatic), and presents most commonly before **two years of age**.
steps.say: A Meckel diverticulum obeys the rule of twos: present in two percent of people, sited two feet from the ileocecal junction, measuring two inches long, carrying two ectopic tissue types (gastric and pancreatic), and presenting before age two.

left.title: Meckel Diverticulum Anatomy
points: True diverticulum (contains all four gut layers)
Arises from antimesenteric border of ileum
Supplied by persistent vitelline artery branch
Often lined by acid-secreting gastric mucosa

right.title: Clinical Complications
points: Painless rectal bleeding from peptic ulceration
Lead point for ileoileal intussusception
Acute diverticulitis mimicking acute appendicitis
Diagnosed by technetium-99m pertechnetate scan

steps.tx: Other vitelline duct anomalies include a vitelline fistula, wherein the entire duct remains patent, causing continuous fecal discharge from the umbilicus. A vitelline cyst forms when both ends obliterate leaving a central fluid-filled sac, while a fibrous **vitelline cord** bridging the ileum to the umbilicus can trap small bowel loops to cause strangulating mechanical obstruction.
steps.say: Other vitelline defects include a patent vitelline fistula discharging fecal matter through the navel, a central vitelline cyst, or a fibrous vitelline cord. A fibrous cord bridging the ileum to the umbilicus can snare bowel coils, producing strangulation.

rows: Acute small bowel volvulus or obstruction

steps.tx: Abdominal wall defects differ fundamentally in embryonic pathogenesis. An **omphalocele** results from failure of the herniated midgut to return to the peritoneal cavity during week ten. The herniated viscera protrude through the midline umbilical ring, covered by a translucent protective membrane composed of amnion externally, Wharton jelly, and peritoneum internally.
steps.say: Ventral wall defects differ fundamentally in origin. An omphalocele occurs when herniated midgut loops fail to return to the abdomen at week ten. The viscera protrude through the umbilical ring encased in a protective sac of amnion and peritoneum.

left.title: Omphalocele Characteristics
points: Defect located directly through umbilical ring
Viscera enclosed within translucent membrane sac
Umbilical cord inserts onto the sac apex
High association with trisomies and Beckwith-Wiedemann

right.title: Gastroschisis Characteristics
points: Full-thickness defect lateral to intact umbilicus
Viscera float completely naked without a sac
Usually on right side of normal cord insertion
Low association with extra-gastrointestinal syndromes

steps.tx: In contrast, **gastroschisis** is a full-thickness defect of the abdominal wall usually situated to the right of an intact umbilicus, caused by vascular disruption of the right omphalomesenteric artery. Viscera eviscerate naked directly into the amniotic cavity without any covering sac, causing severe chemical peritonitis with thickened, edematous, matted bowel loops.
steps.say: In contrast, gastroschisis is a full-thickness abdominal wall defect to the right of an intact umbilicus, caused by vascular disruption. Bowel loops eviscerate directly into amniotic fluid without a covering sac, causing marked chemical peritonitis and serosal thickening.

steps.tx: The diaphragm develops from four distinct embryonic structures: the **septum transversum**, pleuroperitoneal membranes, the dorsal mesentery of the esophagus, and muscular ingrowth from lateral body walls. The septum transversum is a thick plate of cranial mesoderm that forms the central tendon of the adult diaphragm.
steps.say: The diaphragm develops from four distinct embryonic sources: the septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal membranes, the dorsal esophageal mesentery, and body wall muscle ingrowths. The septum transversum forms the central tendon of the diaphragm.

vis.alt: Diaphragmatic embryology, central tendon, crura, and hernia sites
vis.caption: Diaphragm components: septum transversum, pleuroperitoneal membranes, and crura. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Failure of one or both pleuroperitoneal membranes to close the pericardioperitoneal canals results in a congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The most frequent variant is the **Bochdalek hernia**, occurring posterolaterally in eighty-five to ninety percent of cases, predominantly on the left side because the left canal closes later than the right.
steps.say: Failure of pleuroperitoneal membranes to close the pleuroperitoneal canals causes congenital diaphragmatic hernia. The most common type is the posterolateral Bochdalek hernia, occurring on the left side in ninety percent of cases because the left canal closes later.

steps.tx: In Bochdalek hernia, abdominal viscera herniate into the hemithorax, causing severe pulmonary hypoplasia and persistent pulmonary hypertension. The rarer retrosternal **Morgagni hernia** occurs anteromedially between the sternal and costal attachments through the space of Larrey, presenting in late adulthood with mild respiratory distress or retrosternal discomfort.
steps.say: In Bochdalek hernia, herniated abdominal viscera compress developing lungs, causing severe pulmonary hypoplasia. The rarer Morgagni hernia develops anteromedially through the retrosternal space of Larrey, typically discovered as an incidental finding in adulthood.

left.title: Bochdalek Hernia
points: Posterolateral defect (pleuroperitoneal fold)
Eighty-five to ninety percent on the left side
Causes fatal neonatal pulmonary hypoplasia
Scaphoid abdomen with bowel sounds in chest

right.title: Morgagni Hernia
points: Anteromedial retrosternal defect (space of Larrey)
Ninety percent on the right side of sternum
Frequently asymptomatic until adult life
Incidental cardiophrenic mass on chest film
